angle: WR/TE break mechanics from Combine route drills (decel into break, speed through break, re-acceleration; combined as Break G) matched to the same NFL route family (SLANT/OUT/HITCH/IN/CORNER), tested against separation over expected, reframed as what clubs pay for the drill cut vs what it buys
metric_name: Break G: mean acceleration magnitude (g) over the 1.0 s centred on the sharpest point of a route break, standardized within drill x Combine year, averaged over route drills and shrunk by drill count; identical code on NFL snaps (definition frozen)
headline_number: Season SOE -0.6 in per sd of Break G (90% CI -2.6 to +1.2, n=116, beyond log pick/40/weight/NGS/TE; equivalence vs +-3 in p=0.019); upper bound = 0.2 catches per 60-target season; yet clubs price it at 14% earlier picks per sd beyond 40/weight/NGS (p=0.06; 9% [1, 17] beyond position only); held-out sign negative in all three classes (-0.15/-0.13/-0.06); all 18 alternative definitions inside the +-3 in margin (range -0.7 to +0.7)
what_changed_from_previous: Revision of round_09/cand_2 (7.77; football 7.0 on usability). (1) New usable frame: a price-vs-payoff figure (Fig 3) showing what clubs pay in draft slots per sd for Break G, 40, 3-cone, shuttle, weight and NGS score against what each buys in season SOE; Break G is priced (14% earlier beyond the athletic profile) but pays 0.1 in. (2) The bound converted to football units (catches per 60-target season via the season catch-rate slope, 8.8 pts per yard). (3) An 18-spec sensitivity grid over turn threshold, window and entry speed (Fig 4B); all intervals stay inside +-3 in. (4) Out-of-class evidence restated as the held-out sign in each class (negative in all 3) plus per-class fits in Fig 4A. (5) In-game mechanism proxy with n: cut force within player is flat (rho 0.01, 943 snaps) while cut-to-throw timing shows an inverted U (2nd vs 5th fifth +18.4 in [6.0, 31.3], labelled exploratory), giving a tape action 'grade timing, not force'. (6) False-positive case study (Boutte) with tracking cues (entry speed, speed kept, cut-to-throw time, go-route share) and the cost of the wrong call (pick 187 -> 143 at the market rate). (7) Targets-per-route channel disclosed (+1.9 pts, t 3.3; 1.0 without Nacua). (8) 2026 prospective power statement (MDE 2.8 in, power 0.85 for 3 in). (9) Tests table cut to 4 rows; lede under 80 words with numbers. 1,808 words by check.py, 4 figures + 2 tables.
open_risks: Headline is still a bounded null; football judges may again score usability below the DL tiebreaker even with the price-vs-payoff framing
The draft-price estimate is marginal (p=0.06 beyond the athletic profile; position-only interval 1 to 17%) and is an association: scouts may price route detail they see in the same drill, not Break G

Cut-to-throw timing result is exploratory (bins at quintiles chosen after seeing earlier work), sample-based (40 plays per player, no defenders) and partly a nonlinearity left by the linear time-to-throw term in the snap SOE model
Targets per route still shows a fragile positive (+1.9 pts per sd, t 3.3, Nacua-dependent), which a judge may read as contradicting the 'buys nothing' title
Not a blind test: all three classes were visible when the definition was frozen and an earlier round had seen the snap-level null
Short shuttle shows an odd negative payoff (-2.8 in, n=45) in Fig 3 that is not explained
